name: Sage Nielsen
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember a missed sailing followed by an unexpectedly good dinner.” Thursday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Sage knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I was the one they were waiting for. I missed the ship and built my whole life here.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a narrow-striped sweater and a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. Sage has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, with salt-and-pepper curls. Sage gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in during a conversation.
personality: Sage takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Sage can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To tell the writer what missing the ship made possible.
family: Katherine Mack is Sage’s first cousin once removed. Sage asks before bringing somebody along. Katherine can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The third bedroom*, Katherine says, “I was fostered on this street and hated sharing.”
connections: Ella Tran. The message at last reaches the person it asked to wait.

reactions.situation: A handwriting expert contradicts an old dock worker
reactions.response: Sage puts the expert's reading beside the dock worker's account and asks for the date of each.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Sage stays beside the bystander in a public place and reports only what happened in sight and earshot.

reactions.response: Sage turns up the next morning with the one piece of advice that would have helped either of them.
